Original fiction. New series tomorrow night.

scenes.narration: Last time: someone hung the twelfth ornament while Holly slept, and nothing could take it down.
scenes.image: a glowing glass ornament hanging on a dark Christmas tree, frost on the window behind

scenes.narration: Christmas Eve. The house smelled like pine and frost. At dusk the tree lights came on by themselves.
scenes.image: Christmas tree lights flickering on by themselves in a dim living room at dusk

scenes.narration: In the glass, the tall figure had moved. It stood at the tiny front door now. Waiting to be let in.
scenes.image: inside a glass ornament, a tall coated figure standing at a miniature front door

scenes.narration: Holly got a hammer from the garage. She didn't try to take it down. She swung.
scenes.image: woman raising a hammer toward a glowing glass ornament on a Christmas tree

scenes.narration: The ornament burst into a hundred shards of light. The room went cold. Then silent.
scenes.image: glass ornament shattering into glittering shards of light in mid-air

scenes.narration: Then it started to snow. Inside. Out of the ceiling. Soft and slow, settling on the couch, the rug, her hair.
scenes.image: snow falling gently from the ceiling inside a cozy living room onto a Christmas tree and couch

scenes.narration: She laughed. She actually laughed. It was broken. That had to mean something.
scenes.image: woman standing in indoor snowfall, laughing with relief, snowflakes in her hair

scenes.narration: In the morning the snow was gone. The box sat open on the coffee table. She went to throw it out.
scenes.image: antique velvet ornament box open on a coffee table in pale Christmas morning light

scenes.narration: It had thirteen velvet slots now. Eleven ornaments. One pile of broken glass. And the thirteenth, brand new, empty, waiting. Breaking it didn't end it. It just made room.
scenes.image: velvet ornament box with one slot full of broken glass and one new empty slot

scenes.narration: Some calls you can't hang up on. Tomorrow: a 911 dispatcher answers a call from a house with no phone line.
scenes.image: an old rotary telephone on a dusty side table in an empty house, snow outside the window
